supported_general.notes: Exact Git identity, No Active Self-Scan and evidence admission remain foundational general contracts.
General Architecture model contract preserves identity, evidence, observed/inferred/unknown/conflicting posture and claim ceilings. Raw round-trip tooling is not public API.
First completed v1.0 semantic-authority cutover. Legacy Capability Catalog is derived compatibility output only.
L0-L3 progressive disclosure. Query misses do not prove absence.
FlowDefinition/Object, HandoffOccurrence and qualified Assertion semantics are supported for bounded reconstruction/query; there is no Flow truth store.
Stable asset identity, observed roles and explicit owner-evidence posture; no safe-delete authority.
Structural evidence remains non-authoritative for semantic ownership.
Observation absence cannot create retirement/removal/deletion authority.
Evolution remains verified repository change knowledge; Impact remains inferred/predictive and cannot become Architecture fact.
Tracked portable knowledge is independently verified and never self-certifies.

wff_profile_compatibility.notes: WFF-specific trigger/reuse recommendation compatibility; not required by the general Engineering Knowledge Model.
WFF Core contracts and P1/P2/P3/P4/PX semantics remain outside the general meta-kernel.
The fixed WFF v1.6.2 reconstruction profile remains a validated host fixture and compatibility source, not EKRI's general semantic definition.

experimental_internal.notes: Object/Occurrence/Assertion is internal semantic normalization. Normal consumers must not traverse it directly.
Retained as migration/conformance proof infrastructure; not a peer Architecture authority.
Full-scale adversarial authority stress tool, not a normal consumer API.
Release conformance harness; does not create semantic truth.

compatibility_policy.schema: Supported v1 schema identities remain stable within the 1.x compatibility line unless an explicit migration record changes them.
compatibility_policy.api: Supported named queries preserve semantic meaning and claim ceilings; additive fields require compatible defaults, incompatible changes require a major-version decision.
compatibility_policy.profile: WFF-specific compatibility may evolve independently provided general model/query contracts do not acquire WFF-only dependencies.
compatibility_policy.storage: Physical storage or serialization changes do not remint stable semantic IDs by themselves.

rollback_policy.pre_cutover: Discard non-authoritative shadow/derived state and keep the current sole authority.
rollback_policy.post_cutover: Freeze the failed/new context, restore exactly one accepted authority source, rebuild derived views/compatibility outputs, and retain the failed context as historical evidence.

claim_ceiling: This classification defines EKRI v1.0 supported, WFF-profile compatibility and internal/experimental surfaces. It does not make every future Flow, Decision, Claim, Code Graph, runtime trace or domain profile feature-complete, nor does it authorize production governance decisions.
